provenance.source: Vendored verbatim from openstudio-standards NECB2020/data/*.json (tables) and NECB2011/data/curves.json (performance curves); values correspond to NECB 2020 Table 5.2.12.1 minimum performance requirements
provenance.note: Capacity match rule (ported from legacy model_find_object): row matches when minimum_capacity < capacity <= maximum_capacity, retried at 0.99x capacity on boundary misses; criteria keys absent from a row act as wildcards. VERIFIED against the printed NECB 2020 tables via MCP 2026-08-02 and corrected under D-59: unitary_acs and heat_pumps = Table 5.2.12.1.-A exact, including SEER 15 for heat pumps below 19 kW; PTAC rows = Table -G exact (formula coefficient 0.3058/kBtu-h = printed 1.0435/kW unit-converted); heat_pumps_heating = Table -A exact; boilers = Table -N exact; furnaces = Table -O exact (strict-side row choices documented); chillers = Table -K PATH B full-load COPc exact. The 90.1-sourced heat_rejection family left this file under D-89: nothing read it, and the reference tower fan is set by apply_tower_rules from Table 5.2.12.2 plus the 8.4.4.11.(2)-(3) cell rules (D-26). IEER/IPLV/SCOP columns are not modeled: EnergyPlus carries full-load COP plus the reference part-load curves. Those part-load curves are this edition's own since D-89: part_load_fheatplc carries every FHeatPLC class Articles 8.4.5.2. and 8.4.5.3. publish (with a deferred_reason on each class no reference rule elects), part_load_curves maps an equipment class to the curve that represents it, and every boilers and furnaces row declares its part_load_curve_class instead of naming one curve for all of them.

curves.name: BOILER-PLF-MODULATING-necb2020

implements.grid: the ten printed points, PLR 0.10 to 1.00 step 0.10
implements.error_grid: exact at all ten printed points (error 0 by construction); the Code publishes no value between or below them, so there is no exact function to measure an interpolation error against.

curves.notes: Reference modulating boiler part-load factor for Sentence 8.4.5.2.(3), which states that the values for Qpartload/Qdesign and FHeatPLC "shall be those listed in Table 8.4.5.2.-B". The ten printed points are carried verbatim through PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR), so the representation is exact at every value the Code publishes. The Code prints no interpolation rule between them and nothing below PLR 0.10; Linear interpolation and Constant extrapolation are the implementation choices D-89 records. The name is code-qualified because this edition's modulating content is its own (D-88).

curves.name: BOILER-PLF-NONCONDENSING

implements.error_grid: max relative error of the Linear interpolation against the exact rational PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR), sampled at PLR 0.0010 to 1.0000 step 0.0001: 0.1991 % at PLR 0.0014. The grid is finest where the rational is most convex (below PLR 0.05), and the boiler's engine minimum part-load ratio is raised to the first node (0.001) when lower, so every part-load ratio the engine can evaluate lies inside this domain.

curves.notes: Reference non-condensing boiler part-load factor for Article 8.4.5.2. The Code states FHeatPLC as a fuel-INPUT ratio (Fuel_partload = Fuel_design x FHeatPLC), so the EnergyPlus normalized-boiler-efficiency multiplier is PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR) (the D-53 transform). Table:Lookup, Linear interpolation, Constant extrapolation; exact at every node.

curves.name: DXCOOL-REF-COOLEIRFT
curves.notes: Regenerated 2026-07-22 from 8.4.5.4.(7) via the exact degF->degC variable substitution; self-checks to ~1.0 at the 67F wb / 95F odb rating point. Replaces the legacy NECB 2011-derived surface whose twb terms deviated up to 1.95% off-rating (see scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.rb).  Governing requirement in this edition: Article 8.4.5.4.

curves.name: DXCOOL-REF-COOLPLFFPLR
curves.notes: Refit 2026-07-22: least-squares cubic of PLF(PLR) = PLR / EIR_FPLR(PLR) over PLR 0.25-1.0, from the 8.4.5.4.(5) EIR_FPLR cubic. Output clamped to [0.7, 1.0] (PLF > 1 is nonphysical; E+ guidance floor 0.7). A cubic cannot represent the rational target exactly: max implied-EIR deviation ~2.0% (the structural floor; was 3.70% with the legacy 0.7-floored refit). See scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.rb.  Governing requirement in this edition: Article 8.4.5.4.

implements.error_grid: max relative error of the Linear interpolation against the exact rational PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR), sampled at PLR 0.1000 to 1.0000 step 0.0001: 0.0269 % at PLR 0.1049

curves.notes: Reference atmospheric furnace part-load factor for Article 8.4.5.3. The Code states FHeatPLC as a fuel-INPUT ratio (Fuel_partload = Fuel_rated x FHeatPLC), so the EnergyPlus part-load-fraction multiplier is PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR) (the D-53 transform). The grid starts at PLR 0.10 and not at 0.01: EnergyPlus floors a fuel heating coil's PLF at 0.7 (EnergyPlus::HeatingCoils::CalcFuelHeatingCoil, 25.2.0 - "PLF curve values must be >= 0.7. PLF has been reset to 0.7"), and the rational crosses 0.7 near PLR 0.055, so nodes below 0.10 would only feed the engine values it rejects. Below PLR 0.10 the Constant extrapolation holds PLF at 0.788005; the departure from the Code there is bounded by a x Fuel_rated = 1.86 % of rated fuel and is stated in D-89.
